# Do biofilm and planktonic separate?

**The question:** do the samples group by lifestyle, the way we'd hope? The plot
that answers it: a **PCA**, which squeezes thousands of genes into two axes so we can
see which samples are alike.

## Setup {-}

```{r setup04, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- c("data", "../data", "project/data", "../project/data")
data_dir <- data_dir[dir.exists(data_dir)][1]
counts <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "gene_counts.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
meta   <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.tsv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Build a gene × sample matrix, log-transform it, and run the PCA on the samples:

```{r}
mat <- counts %>%
  select(-gene_name) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

logmat <- log2(mat + 1)
logmat <- logmat[rowSums(mat) > 0, ]        # drop genes that are always zero

pca <- prcomp(t(logmat))                     # samples in rows for PCA

# how much variance each axis explains
var_pct <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2), 1)

pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")
```

Now the plot — colour by lifestyle, shape by timepoint:

```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = lifestyle, shape = timepoint)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", var_pct[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_pct[2], "%)"))
```

If biofilm and planktonic land in separate clusters, lifestyle is a strong signal in
the data — exactly what we want before looking for changed genes.

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Principle:</strong> colour and shape let one plot answer two questions at
  once (here: lifestyle <em>and</em> timepoint).
</div>

### 👉 Your turn {-}

Does maturation (timepoint) matter too? Re-colour the points by `timepoint` instead
of lifestyle and see whether the timepoints separate.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>
```{r, eval=FALSE}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = timepoint, shape = lifestyle)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", var_pct[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_pct[2], "%)"))
```
</details>
